title: Grateful Dead Live at Bob Marley Performing Arts Center on 1982-11-26
source: lineage: MSC(Sony TCD-5M) > WAV > SHNrecording:MSC - master soundboard cassette w/ Dolby B by Frank Streeterdigital transfer:Nakamichi CD 2 cassette deck > HHB 850 Pro stand-alone CD burner (16 bit @ 44.1khz) by Frank Streeter and Henry Fishertracking and

ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard capture of the Montego Bay sunrise set, highlighted by a smoking Scarlet / Fire and Fire on the Mountain.
ai_review.review: The streeter SBD source is clean and well‑balanced (aside from a slight speed issue that can be corrected), delivering a listenable recording of an early‑morning festival gig.  The show shines in its brief but memorable second set – the sunrise Scarlet / Fire, Fire on the Mountain and a tight Samson & Delilah are repeatedly praised, while some critics deride a few mis‑steps like Althea>Let It Grow.  Overall the performance is energetic and unique, especially with Jerry’s emotive lead and Brent’s Hammond wizardry.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4‑5 stars and commend the soundboard quality; a minority label it poor, yielding an overall weighted average around 4.2.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Pristine SBD source with clear mix; minor speed/pitch issue noted but easily corrected, no major drop‑outs or buzz in this version.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Short festival set (6‑song first set, sunrise second set) with strong transitions into the iconic Scarlet/Fire and a high‑impact finish; fatigue noted but energy spikes at sunrise.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for emotive lead vocals and guitar tone, especially during the sunrise Fire on the Mountain.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned having fun in the mix, stepping out with funky bass lines; some reviewers note “Phil bombs”.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s Hammond organ work described as tremendous and “rippin’ it” throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey and Bill’s intense drumming highlighted on Fire; overall drum work noted as tight and powerful.
